title: Our intern built a playable 3D platformer on his lunch break and I'm still confused
author: Saikat_Bhattacharya
selftext:
​

So this guy is our video animator, not a coder at all, but he's super into RPGs....like the type to spend his break watching wukong streams and stuff. Walked past his desk yesterday while he was eating and he's just casually got a full 3D action platformer up, characters, movement, all of it, and the part that got me was it actually played.

Turns out he just described the game he wanted in Higgsfield Supercomputer and it did the rest....planned it, wrote all the code, made the assets, even deployed the thing while he sat there with his lunch. FR.

Like 52 minutes from one sentence to something you can genuinely play.

It's still a prototype and not a real finished game, I get that....but for someone who's never written a single line of code in his life to pull this off from just a prompt is kind of nuts to me. Screenshot is roughly where he was at when I caught it.

comments.author: unfamily_friendly
comments.body: This is impressive, but good luck bringing it to completion. The code is probably not maintainable at all and after multiple prompts, AI will stuck in a loop of "Fix A - create error B" "fix B - create error A". This only can work out if a prompter knows how to code. Or if you get extra lucky with prompts

comments.author: dry_garlic_boy
comments.body: Are you joking? This has been easy to do for awhile. It's always a shitty demo game but yes you can do this with almost any decent LLM. You must be really out of touch if you felt the need to post this.
